hard_gates.evidence: The same foreground wearer stands among multiple instructional cooking stations with pots and stools; the board shows bread-stage drawings. This is a practical-class setting rather than costume alone.

The face remains in clear upper-frame view, with a dark chin-length bob, separated fringe, brown eyes and softly rounded contour broadly consistent with the source portrait. This is visual resemblance only; real identity, age and biography remain unknown.

White blouse, navy ribbon and pleated navy skirt remain distinct beneath a pale blue flour-marked bib apron, and neck/waist support is coherent. However the front bow still has a compact central knot and taut folded loops; the required visibly loosening state is not established. Visible garment layers alone cannot pass the full gate.

At native scale both hands are visible gripping folded fabric on opposite sides of the central bow. The subject right hand (image left) holds a folded loop and the subject left hand (image right) holds the other loop away from the knot; neither clearly steadies the central knot while the other pulls a free tail through it. Two free ends still hang below the intact knot. The intended support-plus-free-tail-pull/slackening relation is absent; ordinary bow handling is insufficient.

Flour is visible over the worn apron front, and golden completed bread sits on a cooling rack/tray on the adjacent workbench in the same frame as the wearer. These cues connect clothing and finished practical work without needing the prompt story.

Face, both connected forearms and hands, front waist fastening and bread are all retained in a clear foreground hierarchy. Arms reach the waist coherently and the standing trunk/upper legs are balanced. The physical ownership and reach are readable; the specific unfastening-state defect is recorded separately above.

rule_applied: Every required gate must pass. One partial garment-state gate and one failed complete unfastening relation make this actual-image test FAIL. Criteria unchanged.
impression_before_control_labels: A warm, quiet cooking-class portrait centres the short-haired wearer and flour-covered apron, with finished bread beside her. The expression and slight downward head turn create a calm pause; bow handling is readable but its direction is not the requested release mechanism.
control_comparison: The softly lit everyday presence can plausibly support the intended subtle sensual=1 quality. There is no basis to claim a measured intensity or reference-person desire. Fetish=0 and surreal=0 receive no added treatment. This qualitative impression is separate from the failed action fidelity.
